# CardFields, CardBrandBadges

Card number, expiry, security code and name, formatted as typed: groups of four (4-6-5 for American Express), `MM / YY` with a leading zero added, digits only. The badges dim to the brand detected from the first digits. These inputs are placeholders: a real site swaps the first three for its payment provider’s hosted fields, so card data never passes through its code.

[Live demo](https://gurfi1.github.io/react-shopify-style-checkout/#/blocks/cardfields-cardbrandbadges)

## Usage

```tsx
const [card, setCard] = useState({ number: '', expiry: '', cvc: '', name: '' });

<CardBrandBadges brand={cardBrandOf(card.number)} />
<CardFields value={card} onChange={next => setCard(next)} errors={errors} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `CardValue` | { number, expiry, cvc, name } |
| `onChange` | `(next, field) => void` | The next value, already formatted, and which field changed. |
| `errors` | `Partial<Record<keyof CardValue, string>>` | Messages by field. |
| `onBlurField` | `(field) => void` | Validate on blur here. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | Extra rows under the name field. |
| `CardBrandBadges brand` | `'visa' \| 'mastercard' \| 'amex' \| ''` | The detected brand; the others dim. |

## Files

To use this on its own, copy this folder:

- `CardFields.module.css`
- `CardFields.tsx`

- `brands/` (the card logos and their licence)

It also needs:

- [`src/checkout/CheckoutProvider.tsx`](../CheckoutProvider.tsx)
- [`src/icons`](../../icons)
- [`src/labels.ts`](../../labels.ts)
- [`src/lib/card.ts`](../../lib/card.ts)
- [`src/lib/ids.ts`](../../lib/ids.ts)
- [`src/lib/money.ts`](../../lib/money.ts)
- [`src/primitives/Field`](../../primitives/Field)
- [`src/primitives/FieldError`](../../primitives/FieldError)
- [`src/primitives/Layout`](../../primitives/Layout)
- [`src/primitives/TextField`](../../primitives/TextField)
- [`src/primitives/Tooltip`](../../primitives/Tooltip)
- [`src/types.ts`](../../types.ts)
- [`src/utils.ts`](../../utils.ts)

Everything expects a [`Theme`](../../theme) somewhere above it, which supplies the colours, corners and timings.
